units.translation: unless πρόσωθ᾽ [forward] is to be written with Wakefield.
But they flashed back and passed the word forward
a blazing headland to overpass forward
who sent them forward and brought them back again
you would boast of your race and speak further
to learn of some death-bringing fate further
the man is gone, fleeing forward
but to speak ill of those near, being shapeless, and to stand apart from justice is not lawful
for us to perish, or to assign honors further
And one must know that in Aeschylus (fr. 339) we find προσῳδία [address] used of a salutation, not of the voice with an instrument: "You will not find me inexperienced in this address."
lest someone from afar cast envy of the eye
a god from afar looks upon him kindly
from afar with well-aimed shots being subdued
a god hears even from afar
I heard from afar the cry of a report
let not the vain thing come from chastened faces
they are said to be placed in the front line
προτεγενδι σιγνιφιχατιονε [to stretch forward, to signify]
to hold out, to stretch forth
to hold out, to stretch forth
do not hold out gain to me and then deprive me
hand stretches out from hand, reachings
properly sacrifices before marriage, improperly preludes, skirmishes
where the scholiast is right: κυρίως ταῖς πρὸ γάμου θυσίαις [properly the sacrifices before marriage]; νῦν δὲ ταῖς πρὸ τῆς ἁλώσεως μάχαις [but now the battles before the capture].
δε σαχριφιχιις προ χλασσε οβλατις [sacrifices before the class, offerings]
in the preludes of the spear
aid of wars and preludes of ships
properly the sacrifices before marriage; but now the battles before the capture
εἰ προτέρων αἷμ᾽ [if the blood of earlier ones]
saying gain earlier than later doom
following upon earlier things you have spoken these
for the errors from earlier times
may this end be of earlier women
but justice bids us first to sing the ill-sounding hymn of the Erinys
may no love fall upon the army first
if the blood of earlier ones
to set before oneself, to prefer
Pr. 239 θνητοὺς δ᾽ ἐν οἴκτῳ προθέμενος, τούτου τυχεῖν οὐκ ἠδυνήθην αὐτός. [But having set mortals before me in pity, I could not obtain this myself.]

Φρεθυεντ εν ηυιυς-μοδι λοχυτιονιβυς εστ σιμπλεχς τίθεσθαι [In expressions of this kind the simple τίθεσθαι [to place] is frequent]: χομποσιτο σι υσυς εστ Αεσχυλυς προ πρότερον θέμενος, αντεα μισερότους, διχισσε βιδε-τυρ [Aeschylus seems to have used the compound προθέμενος [having set before] for the simple θέμενος [having placed], that is, having pitied]. Ναυχκιο (Βυλλετιν δε λ'Αχαδεμιε δε Στ. Πε-τερσβουργ αδ. 1860 π. 240) σκριβενδυμ βιδεβατυρ θνητοὺς δ᾽ ἐν οἴκτῳ θέμενος εἶτ᾽ οἴκτου τυχεῖν οὐκ ἠδυνήθην αὐτός. [Nauck (Bulletin de l'Académie de St. Pétersbourg, 1860, p. 240) thought it should be written θνητοὺς δ᾽ ἐν οἴκτῳ θέμενος εἶτ᾽ οἴκτου τυχεῖν οὐκ ἠδυνήθην αὐτός [but having placed mortals in pity, then I could not obtain pity myself].]
